title: The Rule of the Square
subtitle: Calculate pawn races at a glance
description: Determine instantly whether the defending King can catch a runaway passed pawn without King assistance.
theoryNotes: Draw an imaginary square from the pawn to the promotion rank. If the defending King cannot step inside the square on its turn, the pawn promotes untouched.
keyTip: Always advance the pawn immediately (1.a4!) to shrink the square and keep the enemy King outside.

title: Pawn on the 6th Rank
subtitle: Opposition decides win or draw
description: Master the critical 6th-rank threshold where king opposition determines victory or stalemate.
theoryNotes: When the pawn reaches the 6th rank, opposition is decisive. If White holds opposition, the pawn promotes; if Black holds opposition in front of the pawn, it is stalemate.
keyTip: Take the opposition (1.Kb6!) before advancing the pawn to c7.

title: Key Squares
subtitle: Pawn on the 5th rank & outflanking
description: When the pawn is on the 5th rank, its key squares are directly in front of it. Seize the opposition and outflank the defender.
theoryNotes: 1.Ke6! takes the key square in front of the pawn and gains the opposition. Push the pawn only when the King supports it; rushing e6? or e7+ too early can allow stalemate tricks.
keyTip: Play 1.Ke6! and keep the King in front of the pawn.

title: Key Squares: 4th-Rank Pawn
subtitle: Occupy squares two ranks ahead
description: For a pawn on ranks 2-4, key squares are two ranks ahead on the pawn's file and adjacent files (c6, d6, e6 for a d4 pawn). Occupying any key square guarantees a forced win.
theoryNotes: Advance your King to claim c6 (1.Kd5! then 2.Kc6!) before pushing the pawn.
keyTip: Move your King forward to claim c6 (1.Kd5! then 2.Kc6!) before pushing the pawn.

title: Distant Opposition
subtitle: Stop advanced pawns from afar
description: Neutralize an advanced passed pawn by claiming distant opposition on the same file.
theoryNotes: When separated by an odd number of squares (3 or 5), matching the opponent's file takes distant opposition, which converts to direct opposition when the kings close in.
keyTip: Play 1.Kb1! to take distant opposition on the b-file, then 2.Kb2! to hold direct opposition.

title: Rook Pawn Corner Defense
subtitle: Imprisoning the attacking King
description: Lock the attacking King into the corner of the board to force a stalemate draw against a rook pawn.
theoryNotes: A rook pawn cannot promote if the defending king controls the two nearest bishop-file squares (c1 and c2). Locking Black's King on the a-file guarantees stalemate.
keyTip: Play 1.Kc1! and 2.Kc2! to confine Black's King to the rim.

title: Mutual Zugzwang & Trebuchet
subtitle: Reserving the critical attack tempo
description: Win the reciprocal zugzwang battle when both kings attack opposing blocked pawns.
theoryNotes: In the Trebuchet, both kings defend their own pawn while attacking the opponent's. The player whose turn it is to move must give way and lose their pawn.
keyTip: Play 1.Kd5! to reach the Trebuchet with Black to move: 1...Kg4 2.Kxe5 followed by e4-e5-e6-e7.

title: Dual-Purpose King Maneuver
subtitle: The diagonal geometry idea
description: Execute a dual-purpose diagonal King march that hunts an enemy runner while supporting your own pawn.
theoryNotes: Diagonal moves create two simultaneous threats: stepping into the square of Black's h-pawn and assisting the c-pawn to promote.
keyTip: Play 1.Kg7! h4 2.Kf6! Kb6 3.Ke5! threatening both 4.Kd6 and 4.Kf4.

title: Triangulation Maneuver
subtitle: Losing a move to break a fortress
description: Execute triangular King maneuvers (d5-d4-c4-d5) to lose a tempo and hand the move back to the defender, forcing fatal zugzwang.
theoryNotes: 1. Kd5 Kc8 2. Kd4 Kd8 3. Kc4 Kc8 4. Kd5 Kc7 (4... Kd8 5. Kd6 Kc8 6. c7 Kb7 7. Kd7 Ka7 8. Kc6 +- (8. c8=Q stalemate)) 5. Kc5 Kc8 6. Kb6 Kb8 7. Kxa6 Kc7 8. Kb5 +- 1-0.
keyTip: 1.Kd5 Kc8 2.Kd4! Kd8 3.Kc4! Kc8 4.Kd5! Kc7 5.Kc5! Triangulate to reach the starting position with Black to move.

title: Outside Passed Pawn Decoy
subtitle: Diverting the enemy King
description: Advance the distant passed pawn to decoy the enemy King, then infiltrate the opposite flank.
theoryNotes: An outside passed pawn acts as a decoy: the defender must travel to the perimeter to capture it, while your King cleans up the central and opposite pawns.
keyTip: Push 1.h4! immediately; do not let the enemy King blockade the pawn on h2.

title: Tactical Pawn Breakthrough
subtitle: 3 vs 3 pawn sacrifice to queen
description: Execute sacrificial pawn levers to create an unstoppable passed pawn when kings are far away.
theoryNotes: Push 1.b6! into the enemy pawn chain. Regardless of how Black captures, push the opposing flank pawn (2.c6! or 2.a6!) to deflect the remaining defender.
keyTip: 1.b6! axb6 2.c6! bxc6 3.a6! and the a-pawn queens uncontested.

title: 7th-Rank Rook Pawn
subtitle: And Passive Rook vs Rook
description: Defend against a passed rook pawn on the 7th rank when your rook is forced into a passive or flank checking setup.
theoryNotes: The Vancura position: the defending rook anchors from the flank (f6/g6 or b4) and fires horizontal checks whenever the attacking king attempts to shelter.
keyTip: Keep distance between your rook and the enemy King so you cannot be cut off.

title: Basic Rook Endgames
subtitle: Lucena and Philidor
description: The quintessential winning rook endgame technique. Use your rook to build a bridge and shield your King from vertical checks.
theoryNotes: 1. Place your rook on the 4th rank (Rb4). 2. Step your King out of the queening square. 3. Interpose with your rook on the 4th rank when Black checks from behind.
keyTip: Remember: 'Rook to the 4th rank!' (e.g. Rb4). Once checked on the 5th rank, your King steps to the 4th, and Rb4-e4 blocks the check.

title: Intermediate Rook Endings
subtitle: Broaden your knowledge
description: The golden standard for drawing rook endgames down a pawn. Cut off the enemy King from the 6th rank, then give infinite rear checks.
theoryNotes: 1. Keep your rook on the 6th rank (or 3rd rank if Black) to prevent the enemy King from advancing. 2. As soon as the pawn advances, immediately swing your rook to the 1st rank and deliver endless checks from behind.
keyTip: Do not leave the 6th rank until White physically advances their pawn!

title: Practical Rook Endings
subtitle: Rook endings with several pawns
description: Navigate multi-pawn rook endings with active pieces, passed pawn creation, and king activity.
theoryNotes: Tarrasch's rule: Place your rook behind passed pawns, whether attacking or defending. Activity of the rook is worth more than a pawn in 4 vs 3 rook endings.
keyTip: Prioritize rook activity and king centralization over passive pawn defense.

title: Queen vs Rook: Philidor
subtitle: Triangulation & double attack
description: Philidor (1777): White's pieces are ideally placed. Win by Queen triangulation (1.Qe5+ Ka7 2.Qa1+ Kb8 3.Qa5!) to force Black into zugzwang, driving the Rook away to land a decisive double attack.
theoryNotes: 1. Triangulation: White plays 1.Qe5+ Ka7 2.Qa1+ Kb8 3.Qa5! to pass the move back to Black. 2. Zugzwang: The black rook must abandon the king (e.g. 3...Rb1 or 3...Rh7). 3. Double Attack (Fork): After 3...Rb1, 4.Qd8+ Ka7 5.Qd4+ Ka8 6.Qh8+ Ka7 7.Qh7+ forks King and Rook to win 8.Qxb1.
keyTip: Execute the Queen triangle: e5 → a1 → a5! Keep Black's King locked on the rim and watch out for stalemate sacrifices.

title: Queen vs Rook: Herding
subtitle: Solitary rook defense
description: Herding a solitary rook defense from the open center. Coordinate Queen and King to push the defender to the flank, avoid perpetual checks, and convert within 50 moves.
theoryNotes: Under modern time controls, Q vs R frequently ends in 50-move draws when the attacker misplaces the Queen. Use precise geometric checks to herd the defending King to the rim while bringing your King up.
keyTip: Keep the Queen controlling diagonal cross-files and advance your King as soon as the defending King is restricted.

title: Bishop & Knight Checkmate
subtitle: Ending 93: The 10-Step Method
description: Position 13.4: One of the worst starting positions for White. Execute the logical 10-step plan to centralise, force the King to the rim, employ Philidor's W-manoeuvre, build The Cage, and mate in 34 moves.
theoryNotes: 1. Checkmate can ONLY be forced in a corner of your Bishop's square color (here a1/h8). 2. Transfer King and Knight to the center to push the enemy King to a 'Safe Corner' (a8). 3. Occupy the Pivotal Square (c6) with your King. 4. Use Philidor's W-manoeuvre (c7-d5-e7-f5-g7) and the critical barrier move 20.Be3! to prevent escape. 5. Lock the King into 'The Cage' (Position 13.3) and deliver checkmate with two consecutive checks.
keyTip: Checkmating with B+N is logical, NOT mechanical! Take your time at critical moments (moves 16-20) to ensure the defending King cannot slip back into the center.

title: Two Bishops Checkmate
subtitle: Laser wall & king restriction
description: Trap the enemy King between two adjacent bishop diagonals, push it to any edge, and deliver checkmate.
theoryNotes: Bishops work best side-by-side (e.g. d3 and e3) to create an impassable laser wall. Advance your King behind the wall to push the opponent back rank by rank.
keyTip: Bring your King into the action early to cut off escape routes.

title: Rook vs Bishop: Safe Corner
subtitle: Safe corner vs wrong corner
description: Exploit the 'wrong corner' trap where the Bishop's color does not match the corner square to win the piece or deliver mate.
theoryNotes: In Rook vs Bishop, the defending King must run to the 'Safe Corner' (a corner of the OPPOSITE color of their Bishop). If forced into the 'Wrong Corner' (same color as Bishop), they will be mated or lose the Bishop.
keyTip: Trap the King and Bishop on the same diagonal file to win material.
